messages:
Marco (Acme): Hey team — onboarding hit a wall. Our Go microservice (Go 1.20) using the redwood-go-sdk v0.9 is getting intermittent 401s and occasional 429 spikes during env ramp. Happens when we run ~40 goroutines doing parallel generate calls.
Lina (CS): thanks Marco. Can you paste the minimal repro + env (region, auth method)? also are tokens ephemeral or long-lived? :thinking_face:
Marco (Acme): tokens are short-lived (ephemeral) via our auth proxy. Region is us-west-2. Sample request snippet:
```go
client := redwood.NewClient(os.Getenv("REDWOOD_KEY"))
for i := 0; i < 40; i++ {
  go func() {
    resp, err := client.Text.Generate(ctx, req)
    if err != nil { log.Println(err) }
    _ = resp
  }()
}
```
Ravi (Eng): couple immediate asks: 1) are you reusing the client instance across goroutines? 2) any proxy in between terminating idle connections? 3) do you see 401 body like `invalid_token` or `expired_token`?
Marco (Acme): we reuse client yes. Proxy is corporate sidecar that does TLS interception; logs show a 401 body: {"error":"token_mismatch"} not expired. 429s show `rate_limit.concurrency` in headers.
Lina (CS): OK — token_mismatch + concurrency rls suggests token pairing may be wrong when many preflight/handshake attempts happen. Can you share headers dump? also what's the preflight concurrency from your SDK (parallel preflight)?
Marco (Acme): headers dump (sanitized):
```
Authorization: Bearer <ephemeral>
X-Forwarded-For: 10.0.0.12
User-Agent: acme-service/1.2
X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2
```
Ava (Onboard): FYI we've seen corp proxies drop connection reuse, causing the client to re-create handshake and occasionally present a rotated token out of order. Two mitigation paths: 1) ensure SDK caches token and updates atomically; 2) limit goroutine fanout and add jitter/backoff on handshake failures.
Ravi (Eng): quick reproduction idea: set parallelism to 8 instead of 40 and see if 401s vanish. Also enable SDK debug logs with `REDWOOD_LOG=debug` and attach.
Marco (Acme): tried reducing to 8 — 401s dropped to near zero and 429s are much less. Debug log attached (excerpt):
```
[debug] preflight: starting handshake token=abc123 conn=pool-7
[warn] proxy: reset idle conn
[error] auth: token_mismatch status=401
[info] backoff: sleeping 120ms
```
Lina (CS): good signal. Action plan: (1) we recommend short-term: cap parallelism and add client-side exponential jitter (avoid hot burst). (2) medium-term: switch to a token cache holder so in-flight requests all read the same token until swap complete. (3) we'll open an internal ticket to flush guidance for corp-proxy patterns.
Ravi (Eng): also try toggling `Connection: keep-alive` and increasing HTTP2 connection window if your sidecar supports it. If the sidecar closes pooled connections frequently, client may lose token binding context.
Marco (Acme): thanks — we'll try config change + patch to token cache. ETA for full rollout ~tomorrow. One more Q: is there a recommended backoff values doc?
Ava (Onboard): yes — see internal snippet we send on onboarding: start base 50ms, jittered exp backoff up to 1s for token handshake, and cap concurrency to 10 for initial warmup. I'll DM the doc. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: deploy 1745554350 -> staging passed :white_check_mark:
Lina (CS): marking this thread as resolved-if-repro after Marco confirms in staging. Thanks all! :party_parrot:
